subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: being open with the teacher about use [Action]
passage:
Dear Pema Ma'am,
Before I submit my essay on climate and farming, I wanted to tell you how I used an AI tool. I asked it for five angles I could take, and I picked the one on water use. I also asked it to point out grammar mistakes, and I fixed them myself. All the sentences and arguments are mine, and I have attached my rough notes so you can see how the essay grew. I wasn't sure if this is within the rules for the assignment, so I would like to ask you directly. If any of it is not allowed, I'm happy to change it before you mark it. P.S. I would rather ask now than have you wonder later.
Yours sincerely,
Parveen

qa.q: What did Parveen ask the AI tool to do?
qa.a: Parveen asked it for five angles and to point out grammar mistakes.

qa.q: Why did Parveen write to Pema Ma'am before submitting?
qa.a: Parveen was unsure whether it is within the rules, and feels honest but a little nervous, wanting to keep the teacher's trust.

qa.q: What could Parveen do if Pema Ma'am says part of it is not allowed?
qa.a: Parveen could redo that part without the tool and ask what help is acceptable, as the email offers.

qa.q: How might Pema Ma'am see the email?
qa.a: Pema Ma'am is likely to appreciate the openness, since it is easier to guide a student who says how the tool was used.

grounding: A teen tells the teacher the AI was used to brainstorm ideas and check grammar, shows the notes and asks whether that fits the rules.
